lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: After one ugly opener, the Maple Leafs have already found a little backbone - and a little young blood. Toronto's 2-1 win over the Islanders snapped the early wobble and gave the club a 1-1-0 start, good for first in the Atlantic with 2 points. Easton Cowan was the spark, piling up a goal and an assist, while Anthony Stolarz looked like a man determined to make his minutes count again, turning aside 26 shots. That matters in October, when reputations are still being written and mistakes are still fresh. The Leafs are hardly cruising, but they're no longer chasing the game's tone either. Saturday night against Ottawa, they get a clean chance to prove this wasn't a one-night correction but the start of something sturdier.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season died the way too many Toronto seasons have lately - quietly, with the brass promising a cleaner plan and a harder edge. Mark Shapiro backed Vladimir Guerrero Jr. after the comments that set off the week's noise, and that matters because Toronto's offseason still begins and ends with its franchise bat. The Blue Jays finished 79-83 and 5th in the AL East, a flat, unsatisfying line that leaves no room for romance. Guerrero remains the fulcrum; Ross Atkins has already signaled the winter will be about helping him rediscover his timing, not tearing up the whole blueprint. That is the proper instinct. What comes next is the hard part - fixing the lineup, sorting the pitching depth, and deciding whether this front office has the nerve to act like a contender again.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The quiet part of training camp is over - the Raptors have found the loud one. Kawhi Leonard's arrival has already changed the geometry of this team, and the first question in Toronto is no longer whether the talent is there, but whether the shooting around him is sharp enough to matter. Leonard, still being eased in, gives the offense a different spine; Scottie Barnes is eager to learn from him, and that matters in a camp built on hierarchy and habits. The depth chart has some heat, too - young wings Ja'Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles are turning heads, which is exactly how good camps expose the future. Saturday's preseason meeting with Miami will offer the first real glimpse of what this reshaped rotation looks like.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders finally stopped the bleeding - and did it with some bite. Washington's 33-31 upset of the Seahawks gave the club its first real jolt of the season, lifting it to 1-2 and third in the NFC East, just one game back. That matters, because a team that looked flat in losses to Dallas and Philadelphia found some backbone against the defending champions. Marcus Mariota steadied the offense, and the defense - which had been hunting a turnover all month - struck when it had to. Now the hard part: Jayden Daniels is back on the practice field in a limited capacity after the elbow injury, but his status for Sunday in London remains cloudy. What to watch: Daniels' Friday decision and whether Washington can turn one sharp win into a real run against the Colts.

article.title: Cowan, Stolarz Lead Leafs Past Islanders
paragraphs: Easton Cowan and Anthony Stolarz powered the Maple Leafs to a 2-1 win over the Islanders, with Cowan posting a goal and an assist and Stolarz stopping 26 shots. It was Toronto's first win under Jim Hiller, and the Leafs return home Saturday night to face the Senators at 7:00 PM ET on Sportsnet.

For the Blue Jays, the focus stays on the offseason after the club's news conferences, with concessions offered for the lost season and few firm plans set yet. The Raptors are in camp and looking ahead to Saturday's preseason date with the Heat, while their regular season opens Oct. 21 against the Bulls.

In Washington, Jayden Daniels returned to practice in limited fashion, but his status for Sunday's game against the Colts is still uncertain. The Commanders head to London for a 9:30 AM ET kickoff on NFL Network, with Daniels among 10 limited participants in Wednesday's session.
